title: Bakery or cake maker

fields.label: What you bake
fields.help: Bread and pastries, celebration cakes, or both.

fields.label: Everyday bakes
fields.help: What you sell most days and the prices.

fields.label: Celebration cakes
fields.help: Sizes and prices, how many each serves, flavours, fillings, finishes and their extra cost, and how much notice you need.

fields.label: Opening hours
fields.help: Each day of the week, and days you're closed.

fields.label: Brand colour
fields.help: Optional: your shop or box colour.

writerNotes: The hero runs one bake from the side. bake.make loaf for bread bakeries (mix, prove in a basket, shape and score, bake in a glowing oven, cool, first slice showing the crumb) or cake for cake makers (mix, bake in tins, stack, ice, decorate with a drip and berries, slice). Set the colours to match: crust, crumb or sponge, and filling. Write the six stages for that bake with early-morning clock times (or working hours for cakes).

board: four numbers beside the bake. For bread: proving hours, oven temperature, baking minutes, loaves baked. For cakes: layers, oven temperature, minutes, cakes this week. Each with the stages it moves over.

today.bakes: up to eight everyday bakes from the brief with prices and a drawing (boule, tin, baguette, croissant, bun, slab). left is a plausible count for the demo; mark one or two as 0 (sold out). If the brief has no everyday bakes (cakes only), list slices and cupcakes it does sell.

cakes: sizes exactly as priced in the brief (tiers 2 for a tiered cake), with days' notice; sponges, fillings and finishes with their extra cost and natural colours. If the brief has no cakes, offer the brief's large orders (a sharing loaf box, a pastry box) as sizes and keep the finishes plain.
order.hours: Monday to Sunday exactly as the brief gives them; closedWord is the word used for closed days. The order form is a demo: nothing is ordered.

hero.title and hero.titleEm: a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop); today and cakes titles have an italic second half. theme.accent is the bakery's colour, deep enough for white button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav and the footer (short).
